additions.Language Fusion and Contrastive Supervis: The preceding section constructs a visual representation of each candidate and its surrounding scene. Language fusion connects this representation to the fixed descriptions of the benchmark\textquotesingle s event classes, using both attention to phrase embeddings and visual--phrase similarity scores. We also test an auxiliary contrastive objective that encourages the visual representation to align with the descriptions of its positive labels during training. Comparing classification-only and contrastive variants therefore tests the additional alignment objective while retaining language fusion in both models.
additions.Dynamic Class Balancing: Changes to the representation and classifier do not directly determine how strongly each training error contributes to learning. The preceding models use focal loss with fixed class-dependent weights. We next examine whether weighting errors using current predictions and accumulated class difficulty improves road-event recognition. This motivates an FRCB-inspired dynamic class-balancing objective, evaluated through its effects on both common and rare compositions.
additions.Encoder Scaling and Training Partitions: Having defined the contextual experts and their blending procedure, we next examine their performance with a larger pretrained video--text encoder system. The study retains the contextual inputs, expert objectives, blend-selection procedure, and detector-evaluation population. Replacing the paired encoders also requires new cached features and an adjusted text-input projection. This section describes those changes and the training partitions used to separate expert fitting, checkpoint selection, blend selection, and detector evaluation.
